reason: The cited evidence (E1-E4) from a single MD simulation study supports a compression-induced clustering-to-ordering transition at extreme strain rates, but does not provide any evidence linking these ordered regions to dislocation obstruction, microcrack nucleation, or toughness degradation, which are key mechanistic premises of the hypothesis.
premises: High-strain compression induces a clustering-to-ordering transition in Al0.1CrCoFeNi.
This transition involves atomistic rearrangements forming nanoscale ordered regions.
The transition occurs under compressive, not tensile, loading.
The transition is observed in MD simulations at high strain rates (10^10 s^-1).
The ordered regions obstruct dislocations and initiate microcracks, reducing toughness.
